gaps.detail: No lawful ground recorded (§4 requires consent or a §7 legitimate use).
gaps.remediation: Assign a lawful ground to this activity — consent (§4(1)(a)) or a legitimate use (§4(1)(b)/§7). Update the RoPA entry's legal_basis and publish.
gaps.suggestion: Prefer a specific §7 legitimate use where it genuinely applies (e.g. order fulfilment) — it avoids a consent burden the activity doesn't need.

gaps.detail: No retention period set (§8(7)-(8) / Third Schedule requires one per data category).

gaps.suggestion: Align to the Third Schedule class default (e.g. ~3y for e-commerce) unless a law requires longer; document the basis.

citation.title: Special-category / sensitive data
citation.what_it_attests: Where an activity handles sensitive categories, heightened security safeguards (§8(5) + Rule 6) and a documented risk assessment (Rule 13(1)) apply.

gaps.detail: Special-category data present — confirm heightened §8(5)/Rule 6 safeguards and a documented risk assessment.
gaps.remediation: This activity touches sensitive/special-category data — apply heightened safeguards + review the lawful basis and retention.
gaps.suggestion: Minimise: collect the sensitive field only if the purpose truly needs it; encrypt/tokenise at rest.

citation.title: Children's data safeguards
citation.what_it_attests: If any Data Principal is under 18: verifiable parental consent (§9(1) + Rule 10) and an absolute ban on tracking / behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising (§9(3)).

gaps.detail: Data-subject categories suggest children's data but §9 verifiable parental consent / tracking-ban has not been assessed.
gaps.remediation: Determine whether this activity processes children's data (§9); if so, implement verifiable parental consent (Rule 10) + no tracking/targeted ads.
gaps.suggestion: Add an age-signal at collection so children's processing is flagged automatically, not assessed after the fact.

citation.title: Cross-border transfer
citation.what_it_attests: Transfers outside India must be confirmed against the restricted-country list (§16(1); none notified as of 2026-07-01) and any sectoral override (§16(2), e.g. RBI).

gaps.detail: Cross-border transfer present without a §16 recipient/sectoral assessment recorded.
gaps.remediation: Assess whether this activity's processor(s) transfer data outside India (§16); confirm the recipient country isn't restricted and any sectoral override (e.g. RBI).
gaps.suggestion: Record each processor's data-residency + SCCs/equivalent; a foreign SaaS (analytics/marketing) is usually a cross-border transfer.

meta.in_force_note: Substantive DPDP obligations (§3-17, Rule 3/5-15, Third Schedule) take effect 13 May 2027 (Phase 3). Gaps before that date are preparedness gaps, not enforced breaches (reference doc §5, §15).

mandate.title: SDF obligation to undertake periodic DPIA
mandate.what_it_attests: A Significant Data Fiduciary must undertake a DPIA once every 12 months and submit the report + auditor's significant observations to the Data Protection Board.

citation.title: Data Protection Officer
citation.what_it_attests: An India-based DPO reporting to the Board of Directors must be appointed and their contact published (§8(9)).

organisation_gaps.detail: No Data Protection Officer appointed (§10(2)(a) requires an India-based DPO for an SDF).
organisation_gaps.remediation: Appoint an India-based Data Protection Officer reporting to the Board (§10(2)(a)) and publish their contact (§8(9)).
organisation_gaps.suggestion: Register the DPO in the console so the grievance + rights flows route to a real contact.

citation.title: Right to grievance redressal
citation.what_it_attests: A readily-available grievance mechanism with a 90-day response SLA and escalation to the Board must be published.

organisation_gaps.detail: No grievance-redressal mechanism recorded (§13 / Rule 9, 90-day SLA).
organisation_gaps.remediation: Stand up a grievance-redressal mechanism accessible to data principals (§8(10)/§13) with a defined response SLA.
organisation_gaps.suggestion: Wire the My-Data grievance form to the DPO so complaints are tracked + answered within the rule's timeline.

citation.title: Children's data safeguards
citation.what_it_attests: If any Data Principal is under 18: verifiable parental consent (§9(1) + Rule 10) and an absolute ban on tracking / behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising (§9(3)).

organisation_gaps.detail: Whether the tenant processes children's data has not been assessed (§9 / Rule 10).
organisation_gaps.remediation: Assess org-wide whether any activity processes children's data (§9 + Rule 10); if none, record the determination.
organisation_gaps.suggestion: A documented 'we do not process children's data' finding is itself a valid, defensible DPIA outcome.

citation.what_it_attests: A 30/60-day access mechanism (summary of processing + recipients, first request free/year) must be live.

citation.title: Right to correction & erasure

citation.title: Right to nominate
citation.what_it_attests: A Data Principal may nominate another to exercise their rights on death or incapacity.

breach_citation.title: Personal data breach notification
breach_citation.what_it_attests: A breach-notification capability must exist: to the Board 'without delay' + detailed report within 72 hours, and to affected Data Principals 'without delay' in plain language.

citation.title: Algorithmic due diligence
citation.what_it_attests: Where algorithms process personal data, the SDF must verify they are not likely to pose a risk to Data Principal rights.

content.note: Rule 13(3) due-diligence applies where algorithms process personal data; assess per deployed system.
